components.note: Originally a drawing of a person's head with the body below, which is why 页 sits in head-related characters like 头 and 顶; the 'page' meaning is a later extension.

example.pinyin: Qǐng fān dào dì shí yè.
example.english: Please turn to page ten.
example.fact: 页 counts the pages of a book (第十页) and has carried over to the digital world: 网页 is a web page and 首页 is a home page. It is a different word from 叶 (leaf), which is pronounced exactly the same, yè.

components.note: 氵 (water) — bubbles and soaking both involve liquid
包 (bāo) gives a rough sound hint — similar vowel, different initial and tone from pào

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng pào bēi chá.
example.english: I want to make a cup of tea.
example.fact: 泡 as a verb means to soak or steep, so you 泡茶 (brew tea), 泡面 (make instant noodles) or 泡温泉 (soak in a hot spring). The reading pāo is a different word meaning puffy or spongy, so check the tone before you say it.

components.note: 代 (dài) gives the sound — same syllable and tone as 袋
衣 (clothing) — bags were first made of cloth

example.pinyin: Wǒ de dàizi hěn zhòng.
example.english: My bag is very heavy.
example.fact: 袋 usually shows up with a suffix or partner: 袋子 (bag), 口袋 (pocket), 塑料袋 (plastic bag). It also works as a measure word for bagged goods, as in 一袋米 (a bag of rice). 袋鼠 is the word for kangaroo, literally 'pouch rat'.

components.note: 石 (stone) — hardness is pictured through stone
更 (gèng) gives a loose sound hint — same -eng/-ing ending but a different initial

example.pinyin: Zhège miànbāo tài yìng le.
example.english: This bread is too hard.
example.fact: 硬 is the opposite of 软 (ruǎn, soft), and it extends beyond texture: 硬座 is a train's hard seat, 硬盘 is a hard drive, and 硬要 means to insist stubbornly on doing something.

components.note: 氵 (water) — an old sense is controlling water, as in taming rivers
台 (tái) — the other part; in modern readings it gives little sound clue

example.pinyin: Yīshēng néng zhìhǎo nǐ de bìng.
example.english: The doctor can cure your illness.
example.fact: 治 covers two worlds: running a state (政治, 治国) and treating illness (治病, 治疗). The legend of 大禹治水, Yu the Great taming the floods, shows the water radical's original link to managing rivers.

components.note: Usually explained as a craftsman's tool, with some seeing a carpenter's square, standing for skilled manual work.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zài gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
example.english: My dad works in a factory.
example.fact: 工 rarely stands alone in modern Chinese; it builds words such as 工作 (job), 工人 (worker), 工资 (wages) and 打工 (to work a casual or part-time job). It is also the radical in 左, 巧 and 差.

components.note: Old forms are often read as a hanging musical bell or a similar object; the meaning 'south' was borrowed, so the picture does not literally show a direction.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài chéngshì de nánbian.
example.english: My home is on the south side of the city.
example.fact: Chinese lists the directions as 东南西北 (east, south, west, north), not north-south-east-west. A compass is 指南针, literally the 'south-pointing needle', and 南 appears in 南方 (the south) and 南京 (Nanjing, 'southern capital').

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, the setting for the old sense of a deep inner corner
米 (rice) — a part of the shape, not a clue to the meaning
大 (big) — the bottom part, completing the decomposition

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de nèiróng hěn shēn'ào.
example.english: The content of this book is very profound.
example.fact: 奥 almost never stands alone. It appears in 深奥 (profound), 奥妙 (mystery, subtlety), 奥运会 (the Olympics) and 奥地利 (Austria). Its oldest meaning was the deep inner corner of a house, which fits the idea of something hidden and hard to reach.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — permission and promises are given in words
午 (wǔ) gives a loose sound hint — shared -u ending

example.pinyin: Tā yěxǔ míngtiān huì lái.
example.english: Maybe he will come tomorrow.
example.fact: 许 mostly lives inside compounds: 也许 and 或许 (perhaps), 允许 (to permit), 许多 (many). It is also a common surname, Xǔ, and can mean 'to promise', as in 许愿 (to make a wish).

components.note: 取 (qǔ) — 'to take', and it also gives the exact sound
女 (woman) — the woman being taken as a wife

example.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào qǔ tā.
example.english: He is going to marry her next year.
example.fact: Chinese has separate verbs for each side of a wedding: a man 娶 (takes) a wife, a woman 嫁 (jià) marries into a husband's family. You cannot swap them; in English both are just 'to marry'.

components.note: Commonly described as a person with decoration or tattoos on the chest, the root of 文身 (tattoo) and later of 'patterns' and 'writing'.

example.pinyin: Nǐ huì xiě Zhōngwén ma?
example.english: Can you write Chinese?
example.fact: 文 names languages in their written form: 中文, 英文, 日文. 语, as in 汉语 and 英语, leans toward the spoken language, though the two are often interchangeable. 文 also underlies 文化 (culture) and 文明 (civilization).

components.note: 其 (qí) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone
月 (moon) — the moon measured time in months, hence time periods

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn qīdài zhè cì lǚxíng.
example.english: I'm really looking forward to this trip.
example.fact: 期 turns up in time words: 星期 (week), 日期 (date), 学期 (semester), 假期 (holiday). It can also be a measure word for issues or installments, as in 第三期. 期待 means to look forward to something with anticipation.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — the old money radical; the link to sticking is only historical
占 (zhàn) gives a loose sound hint — shared -an/-ie is not close, so treat it as a memory aid

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhàopiàn tiē zài zhèlǐ.
example.english: Please stick the photo here.
example.fact: 贴 means to stick something flat onto a surface: 贴纸 is a sticker and 贴邮票 is to put on a stamp. 贴心 literally 'close to the heart', describes someone considerate. Online, 贴 is also used for forum posts, as in Baidu's 贴吧.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — interjections and particles are things you voice aloud
约 (yuē) gives a loose sound hint — the vowel differs, so it is mostly a memory aid

example.pinyin: Yō, nǐ jīntiān chuān de zhēn piàoliang!
example.english: Oh, you look really pretty today!
example.fact: 哟 expresses mild surprise, often with a teasing or admiring edge. At the end of a sentence it can soften the tone as a light particle (neutral tone yo), as in songs and lively speech: 加油哟 (come on!).

components.note: 廴 (long stride) — a movement radical, tied to the idea of carrying something forward
聿 (yù) is the other half; in modern jiàn it gives little sound clue

example.hanzi: 他们在河边建了一座桥。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài hé biān jiàn le yí zuò qiáo.
example.english: They built a bridge by the river.
example.fact: 建 suits large or formal constructions and institutions: 建国 (found a country), 建立 (establish), 建筑 (architecture). It also gives 建议, 'suggestion'. For an ordinary house, speakers often use 盖 (gài) instead.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the ridgepole was a main timber beam
东 (dōng) gives the sound — close, differing only in the tone

example.pinyin: Nà dòng lóu yǒu sānshí céng.
example.english: That building has thirty floors.
example.fact: 栋 is the measure word for buildings: 一栋楼, 一栋房子. Its original meaning is the ridgepole, the main beam of a roof, which is why it counts whole buildings. 幢 (zhuàng) is a close alternative for the same job.

components.note: A drawing of a tree: a trunk with branches above and roots below.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì mùtou zuò de.
example.english: This table is made of wood.
example.fact: 木 is the 'wood' element in the Five Elements (五行: metal, wood, water, fire, earth). It rarely stands alone: 木头 (wood), 树木 (trees), 木材 (timber). It can also mean numb, as in 麻木.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — things gathered inside a boundary
才 (cái) — in the simplified form this replaced the right half of 團, a stand-in rather than a meaning clue

example.hanzi: 我们跟旅行团去了日本。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen gēn lǚxíngtuán qù le Rìběn.
example.english: We went to Japan with a tour group.
example.fact: 团 means both 'round ball' and 'group': 饭团 (rice ball), 旅行团 (tour group), 团队 (team). 团圆 means a family reunion, and the 团圆饭 is the New Year's Eve dinner. It is the simplified form of 團.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — the old sense was boiling raw silk until it became soft and pure
柬 (jiǎn) gives a loose sound hint — the -an ending is shared, the initial is not

example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān liànxí xiě Hànzì.
example.english: I practice writing Chinese characters every day.
example.fact: 练 is for building skills through repetition: 练习 (practice), 训练 (training), 练字 (practice calligraphy). Do not mix it up with 炼 (liàn, to smelt or refine), which sounds the same; 锻炼 'exercise' uses that one.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early bridges were built of timber
乔 (qiáo) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo yǒu yìbǎi nián le.
example.english: This bridge is a hundred years old.
example.fact: Bridges take the measure word 座 (一座桥). The idiom 过河拆桥, 'tear down the bridge after crossing the river', describes someone who abandons the people who helped them. 桥 also names the card game bridge: 桥牌.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — an action radical, linked to the old sense of leading or guiding
由 (yóu) — the other part, which does not give a clear meaning or sound clue

example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān qù Díbài lǚxíng.
example.english: We're going to Dubai tomorrow.
example.fact: In modern Chinese 迪 mainly appears in transliterated foreign names: 迪拜 (Dubai), 迪士尼 (Disney), 迪斯科 (disco). Its original meaning, to guide or enlighten, survives in 启迪 (to inspire).

excludeSuggestion: Hardly ever a standalone word; used mainly in transliterations of foreign names.

components.note: 石 (stone) — weights for a balance were once stones, which fits the 'standard weight' sense
马 (mǎ) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.hanzi: 请告诉我你的手机号码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ.
example.english: Please tell me your phone number.
example.fact: 码 is behind many words for numbers and codes: 号码 (number), 密码 (password), 二维码 (QR code), 代码 (source code) and 尺码 (clothing size). It is also the unit 'yard' in measurements.

components.note: Commonly read as a mineral pellet in a mining pit: cinnabar, the red ore prized for pigment and alchemy.

example.hanzi: 古人相信吃丹药可以长生不老。
example.pinyin: Gǔrén xiāngxìn chī dānyào kěyǐ chángshēng bùlǎo.
example.english: People in ancient times believed that taking elixir pills could grant immortality.
example.fact: 丹 was originally cinnabar, a red mineral. Daoist alchemists made 丹药 (elixirs) from it in the hope of immortality, and 丹田 names the energy center below the navel. It also appears in 牡丹 (peony) and 丹麦 (Denmark).

components.note: 亻 (person) — the character refers to a person
尹 (yǐn) gives a loose sound hint — same vowel, different ending and tone

example.pinyin: Tā qùnián qù guo Yīlǎng.
example.english: He went to Iran last year.
example.fact: In modern Mandarin 伊 appears mostly in transliterated names: 伊朗 (Iran), 伊拉克 (Iraq), 伊斯兰教 (Islam). In Taiwanese Hokkien it is still an everyday word for 'he' or 'she'.

excludeSuggestion: Mostly seen in transliterated names and literary use; rare as an everyday standalone word.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — proving something is done by words and testimony
正 (zhèng) gives the sound — identical, and it also means 'correct, true'

example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nǐ de shēnfènzhèng.
example.english: Please show your ID card.
example.fact: 证 is the word on many documents: 身份证 (ID card), 学生证 (student card), 证件 (documents) and 证明 (to prove). Note the homophones 证, 症 (symptom) and 政 (politics); context and the radical tell them apart.

components.note: A woman figure (女) with two dots marking breasts, picturing a nursing mother.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de mǔqīn shì lǎoshī.
example.english: My mother is a teacher.
example.fact: 母亲 is the formal word for mother, while 妈妈 is the everyday one. 母 also marks females of animals (母鸡, hen) and appears in 母语 (native language) and 母校 (one's alma mater).

components.note: 龶 — the upper plant-like shape, from the grain stalk in the original 麥
夂 (foot) — a downward foot; the traditional form adds a foot to the old wheat picture

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zhòng le hěn duō xiǎomài.
example.english: A lot of wheat is grown here.
example.fact: 麦 is the grain: 小麦 (wheat), 大麦 (barley), 麦子, 麦片 (oatmeal). Many scholars note that 来 (come) began as a drawing of a wheat plant, so the 'come' and 'wheat' characters are old relatives. Be careful not to mix up 麦 mài, 买 mǎi and 卖 mài.

components.note: 亦 (yì) replaced the complex top of 戀 in simplification — a stand-in, with no real sound link
心 (heart) — the feeling of attachment and love

example.hanzi: 他们谈恋爱已经三年了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen tán liàn'ài yǐjīng sān nián le.
example.english: They have been together for three years.
example.fact: 恋 sits mostly in compounds: 恋爱 (romantic love), 初恋 (first love), 失恋 (heartbreak), 恋人 (lover). 谈恋爱 literally 'to talk about romance' is the everyday way to say 'to be dating'. You say 我爱你, not 我恋你.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — the original meaning is the warp threads of a loom
巠 (jīng) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù jīngguò wǒ jiā.
example.english: This road passes by my house.
example.fact: 经 originally meant the lengthwise threads of fabric, the warp; 纬 was the weft. That is why 经度 and 纬度 are longitude and latitude. The meaning grew to 'to pass through' (经过), 'to experience' (经验), and 'classic' (佛经, sutra).

components.note: 忄 (heart) — an emotional or painful state
参 (cān) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Tā shū de hěn cǎn.
example.english: He lost badly.
example.fact: 惨 is often used after 得 to say something went terribly: 输得很惨 (lost badly). Colloquially 我惨了 means 'I'm doomed', and 太惨了 is an exclamation of sympathy. The related 悲惨 is a more formal tragic word.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — lifting is a hand action
台 (tái) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.hanzi: 请帮我抬一下这张桌子。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ tái yíxià zhè zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: Please help me lift this table.
example.fact: 抬 is used for lifting something up, and for two or more people carrying a heavy thing between them. 抬头 means to raise one's head. In colloquial speech 抬杠 describes arguing just for the sake of arguing.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — a blade
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound hint — the -ian ending is shared, the initial differs

example.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiù xǐhuan liàn jiàn.
example.english: He has loved practicing swordsmanship since childhood.
example.fact: 剑 is the straight, double-edged sword, unlike the single-edged 刀 (dāo). The pair appears in the idiom 刀光剑影, 'flash of blades and shadow of swords', for tense fighting, and 剑 gives 剑桥 (Cambridge).

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the original idea is a width of fabric
畐 (fú) gives the sound; the same part also appears in 福 fú and 副 fù

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yì fú huà.
example.english: A painting hangs on the wall.
example.fact: 幅 is the measure word for paintings, photos, maps and posters: 一幅画, 一幅地图. 张 also works for flat things, but 幅 feels more artistic. It also builds 幅度 (range, extent) and 篇幅 (length of a text).

components.note: 氵 (water) — pouring liquid into something
主 (zhǔ) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Qǐng zhùyì ānquán.
example.english: Please pay attention to safety.
example.fact: 注 is the core of 注意 (pay attention), 注射 (to inject), 注册 (to register), 关注 (to follow closely, or follow someone online) and 注释 (annotation). The idea of 'pouring' attention in explains the modern uses.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth, with lines above for words coming out

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué yì mén xīn yǔyán.
example.english: I want to learn a new language.
example.fact: 言 is a classical word for speech and survives in compounds: 语言 (language), 发言 (to speak up), 留言 (leave a message), 方言 (dialect). It is the source of the 讠 radical used in many speaking characters.

components.note: 足 (foot) — stepping is done with the foot
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.hanzi: 对不起,我踩到你的脚了。
example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ cǎi dào nǐ de jiǎo le.
example.english: Sorry, I stepped on your foot.
example.fact: 踩 means to put your foot down on something. It has a lively slang life: 踩雷 ('step on a mine') means to pick something disappointing, such as a bad restaurant, and 踩坑 is similar.

components.note: 刃 (rèn) — a blade, and its sound is close to rěn
心 (heart) — the blade sits above the heart, an image of enduring pain

example.pinyin: Wǒ rěnbuzhù xiào le.
example.english: I couldn't help laughing.
example.fact: 忍不住 means 'can't help doing' something. 忍 also builds 忍耐 (endure) and 残忍 (cruel). A line from the Analects, 小不忍则乱大谋, says a lack of patience in small things ruins big plans.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — the original idea is a pattern woven into silk
文 (wén) gives the sound — identical, and it also means 'pattern, markings'

example.hanzi: 他的手臂上有一个纹身。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒubì shàng yǒu yí gè wénshēn.
example.english: He has a tattoo on his arm.
example.fact: 纹 means the lines or patterns on a surface: 皱纹 (wrinkles), 指纹 (fingerprint), 花纹 (decorative pattern), 纹身 (tattoo). It rarely stands alone.

components.note: 亻 (person) — an upright person
匕 — an upside-down person, so the pair shows a person changing

example.pinyin: Bīng huà chéng shuǐ le.
example.english: The ice melted into water.
example.fact: 化 works like the English suffix '-ize' or '-ification': 现代化 (modernization), 全球化 (globalization), 文化 (culture). Alone it means to change or melt, and it is also in 化学 (chemistry) and 化妆 (to put on makeup).

components.note: 刀 (knife) — a cutting tool
前 (qián) gives a loose sound hint — same -ian vowel, different initial

example.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù jiǎn tóufa.
example.english: I'm going to get a haircut.
example.fact: 剪 is cutting with scissors, in contrast with 切 (qiē, to cut with a knife). 剪刀 means scissors, 剪纸 is the folk art of paper-cutting, and 剪辑 is editing video.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting something apart, as in a judgment
半 (bàn) gives the sound — close, and it also means 'half', as in splitting a case

example.pinyin: Fǎguān pàn tā yǒu zuì.
example.english: The judge found him guilty.
example.fact: 判 appears in the language of courts and decisions: 判断 (to judge), 判决 (verdict), 审判 (trial), 判刑 (to sentence). Its idea of dividing in half connects to deciding between two sides.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body parts use this flesh radical
匈 (xiōng) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Wǒ de xiōngkǒu yǒudiǎn téng.
example.english: My chest hurts a little.
example.fact: 胸 can be physical, 胸口 (chest), or figurative, as in 胸怀 (breadth of mind). The idiom 胸有成竹, 'to have a complete bamboo in one's chest', means to be confident and well prepared.

components.note: 火 (fire) — an explosion or burst of heat
暴 (bào) gives the sound — identical in pinyin, and it also means 'violent'

example.pinyin: Qìqiú bào le.
example.english: The balloon burst.
example.fact: 爆 also has slang uses: 爆满 (completely packed), 爆火 (to go viral) and 爆款 (a hit product). In cooking, 爆炒 means to stir-fry quickly over a very high flame.

meanings: to hold up on the palm

components.note: 扌 (hand) — lifting or supporting by hand
乇 — a rare part whose sound (zhé) is only a loose match to tuō

example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu tuō zhe xiàba.
example.english: He rests his chin on his hand.
example.fact: 托 means to support something from beneath with your palm: 托盘 (tray). It also builds 委托 (to entrust), 托福 (the TOEFL exam, also 'thanks to your good fortune') and 拜托, a polite way to ask for a favor.

components.note: 虫 (creepy-crawly) — snakes were grouped with small creatures
它 (tā) gives a loose sound hint; 它 was originally a drawing of a snake itself

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn pà shé.
example.english: I am very afraid of snakes.
example.fact: 蛇 is the sixth animal of the Chinese zodiac and counts with the measure word 条 (一条蛇). The idiom 画蛇添足, 'draw a snake and add feet', warns against spoiling something by adding unnecessary extras.

components.note: The shape mixes strokes like 千 and 北, but it does not reliably hint at the meaning, so it is best learned as a whole.

example.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn guāi.
example.english: This child is very well-behaved.
example.fact: 乖 is the praise parents give children and pets who listen: 乖孩子, 真乖. It is also an affectionate way to call out 乖 (good girl, good boy). In older Chinese it meant 'contrary, at odds' (乖僻), the reverse of today's use.

components.note: Two people standing back to back, which is the root of both 'to turn one's back' and 'north'.

example.pinyin: Běijīng zài Zhōngguó de běifāng.
example.english: Beijing is in the north of China.
example.fact: 北 began as two people back to back and gave the sense 'to turn one's back', as in 败北 (to be defeated). It also came to mean 'north', since buildings traditionally faced south with their backs to the north.

components.note: 月 — here a boat or body-shaped part, not the moon, in the traditional analysis
卩 (kneeling person) — a person submitting
又 (hand) — a hand pressing, the old image of making someone submit

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn piàoliang.
example.english: This piece of clothing is very pretty.
example.fact: 服 appears in 衣服 (clothes), 服务 (service), 服从 (to obey), 舒服 (comfortable), 佩服 (to admire) and 服药 (to take medicine). In 衣服 the second syllable is a neutral tone, fu.

components.note: 糸 (silk thread) — ties and connections run along threads

example.hanzi: 他在大学的历史系教书。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué de lìshǐ xì jiāoshū.
example.english: He teaches in the university's history department.
example.fact: 系 xì is the word for a university department (中文系, 历史系), and builds 系统 (system), 关系 (relationship) and 联系 (contact). Read jì, it means to tie: 系鞋带 (tie shoelaces), 系领带 (tie a tie).

components.note: 目 (eye) — the eye, damaged in the original sense
害 (hài) — 'to harm', also giving a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Bié xiā shuō!
example.english: Don't talk nonsense!
example.fact: 瞎 literally means blind, but it is more often an adverb for doing something with no basis: 瞎说 (talk nonsense), 瞎猜 (guess wildly), 瞎忙 (be busy for nothing). 瞎子 for a blind person is considered impolite; 盲人 is neutral.
